correctness.rationale: The weighted semigroup generators at weighted degree 1 have s-exponents 1..d and at degree e have 0..e−1. The intervals for h weight-e generators concatenate to precisely j∈[a mod e, da], proving the claimed membership formula. Since t^d is integral and lies in the fraction field, the d-th Veronese B is the normalization. A monomial m(a,j) multiplies every B-monomial into R iff j≥e−1, giving the sharp conductor and nonnormal line u↦u^e. The eventual-multiple criterion yields the displayed seminormalization and e≤2 boundary. p-root closure of this semigroup yields Frobenius splitting iff e=1 or e=2 with p odd; explicit missing monomial (e−1,e−2) shows e≥3 always fails. Independently generated 840 degree/parameter semigroup comparisons and conductor cases agreed. This is an unrestricted semigroup proof, not inference from finite trials.
residual_risks: No assertion for all weighted determinantal scrolls. Direct finite tests do not prove all parameter values.

value.rationale: The weighted rational cones are a natural, published two-parameter family. Their precise nonnormal conductor, seminormalization and Frobenius-purity regimes distinguish degeneration behavior not captured by normality or Hilbert series. e=2 yields a substantive nonnormal-but-F-split phenomenon exactly in odd characteristic; this is a compact useful exact classification, although methods use known monoid criteria.
residual_risks: General theoretical tools are classical; value is in the natural family-specific phase and scheme boundary, not a general new purity criterion.

limitations: Algebraically closed k, d≥2,e≥1; Frobenius claims positive char only; no all-scroll classification.
